summary: A survey of 2,778 AI researchers predicts AI systems have a 50% chance of hitting milestones by 2028 and of outperforming humans in all tasks by 2047, 13 years earlier than last year's estimate. Respondents are divided on whether faster progress is good, many assign meaningful probability to catastrophic outcomes, and most agree AI risk research should be prioritized.

claims.text: The survey is the largest of its kind, with 2,778 AI researchers who published in top-tier venues.
claims.evidence_quote: In the largest survey of its kind, 2,778 researchers who had published in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) venues gave predictions on the pace of AI progress and the nature and impacts of advanced AI systems

claims.text: Respondents give at least a 50% chance that by 2028 AI systems will autonomously construct a payment processing site, create a song indistinguishable from a popular musician's new song, and autonomously download and fine-tune a large language model.
claims.evidence_quote: at least a 50% chance of AI systems achieving several milestones by 2028, including autonomously constructing a payment processing site from scratch, creating a song indistinguishable from a new song by a popular musician, and autonomously downloading and fine-tuning a large language model.

claims.text: If science continues undisrupted, there is a 10% chance of unaided machines outperforming humans in every task by 2027 and a 50% chance by 2047.
claims.evidence_quote: If science continues undisrupted, the chance of unaided machines outperforming humans in every possible task was estimated at 10% by 2027, and 50% by 2047.

claims.text: The 50% estimate for machines outperforming humans in every task is 13 years earlier than the estimate from a similar 2022 survey.
claims.evidence_quote: The latter estimate is 13 years earlier than that reached in a similar survey we conducted only one year earlier [Grace et al., 2022].

claims.text: All human occupations becoming fully automatable is forecast to reach 10% chance by 2037 and 50% by 2116, compared to 2164 in the 2022 survey.
claims.evidence_quote: the chance of all human occupations becoming fully automatable was forecast to reach 10% by 2037, and 50% as late as 2116 (compared to 2164 in the 2022 survey).

claims.text: 68.3% of respondents think good outcomes from superhuman AI are more likely than bad outcomes.
claims.evidence_quote: 68.3% thought good outcomes from superhuman AI are more likely than bad

claims.text: Among net optimists, 48% gave at least a 5% chance of extremely bad outcomes such as human extinction.
claims.evidence_quote: of these net optimists 48% gave at least a 5% chance of extremely bad outcomes such as human extinction

claims.text: Among net pessimists, 59% gave at least a 5% chance of extremely good outcomes.
claims.evidence_quote: 59% of net pessimists gave 5% or more to extremely good outcomes.

claims.text: Between 38% and 51% of respondents gave at least a 10% chance that advanced AI leads to outcomes as bad as human extinction.
claims.evidence_quote: Between 38% and 51% of respondents gave at least a 10% chance to advanced AI leading to outcomes as bad as human extinction.

claims.text: More than half of respondents said substantial or extreme concern is warranted about six AI-related scenarios, including misinformation, authoritarian control, and inequality.
claims.evidence_quote: More than half suggested that "substantial" or "extreme" concern is warranted about six different AI-related scenarios, including misinformation, authoritarian control, and inequality.

claims.text: Respondents disagreed about whether faster or slower AI progress would be better for humanity's future.
claims.evidence_quote: There was disagreement about whether faster or slower AI progress would be better for the future of humanity.

claims.text: There was broad agreement that research aimed at minimizing potential risks from AI systems ought to be prioritized more.
claims.evidence_quote: However, there was broad agreement that research aimed at minimizing potential risks from AI systems ought to be prioritized more.
